newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKEES SIGN LEFTY RELIEVER STANTON.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKEES SIGN LEFTY RELIEVER STANTON.

text.p: The New York Yankees signed free agent left-handed reliever Mike Stanton to a three-year contract, the World Series champions announced on Wednesday.
Terms were not disclosed, but reports estimated the deal to be worth $5.3 million.

Stanton provides the Yankees with a valuable left-hander in the bullpen and insurance in case closer John Wetteland leaves via free agency and set-up man Mariano Rivera is asked to step up to the closer's role.
Wetteland, the World Series MVP, is seeking a three-year deal worth about $6 million a year.
The 29-year-old Stanton was 4-4 with one save and a 3.66 ERA in 81 appearances with Boston and Texas last season.

Stanton has been used primarily as a setup man and middle reliever in his eight-year major league career. He has a career 23-25 record with a 3.92 ERA in 407 relief appearances for Atlanta (1989-95) Boston (1995-96) and Texas (1996).

Meanwhile, speculation continues to swirl about the possibility of three-time Cy Young award winner Roger Clemens joining the Yankees. The long-time Boston Red Sox ace, now a free agent, is also being courted heavily by the Cleveland Indians, Chicago White Sox.
Clemens is reportedly seeking a four-year contract worth about $7 million a year. The Red Sox have offered him a four-year deal worth $24 million.

The Yankees, who lost free agent starter Jimmy Key to Baltimore, are also interested in Baltimore's free agent pitcher David Wells, who is seeking a three-year deal worth about $14 million. The Indians is interested in Wells as well.
